catalog.name: coffee-sandbox
catalog.description: How to reach and operate the "coffee" sandbox — the dedicated remote machine for unipi v3 development and testing (Tailscale, key-based SSH, omniroute bridge with the full model catalog, sleep-proofed for lid close). Use this skill whenever the user wants to test unipi on coffee, SSH into coffee, deploy code there, run pi/unipi remotely, or troubleshoot coffee's connectivity, sleep/lid behavior, or model availability. Includes exact aliases, the sudo password handling, and the gotchas from initial setup.

catalog.name: compactor-doctor

catalog.name: compactor-stats

catalog.name: configure-notify

catalog.name: configure-updater

catalog.name: consolidate

catalog.name: consultant

catalog.name: council-mode

catalog.name: debug

catalog.name: docker-debug

catalog.name: document

catalog.name: fix

catalog.name: grill-me

catalog.name: handoff

catalog.name: image

catalog.name: kanboard-doctor

catalog.name: memory

catalog.name: milestone-onboard
catalog.description: Create MILESTONES.md from existing workflow docs — scan, propose, refine, write.

catalog.name: milestone-update

catalog.name: mise
catalog.description: Provides expert guidance on mise (mise-en-place) — a polyglot dev tool and environment orchestrator that manages runtimes, environment variables, and project tasks. This skill should be used when users ask about mise configuration (mise.toml), installing or switching tool versions (Node, Python, Go, .NET, etc.), the mise task runner, environment variable management, secrets with SOPS/fnox, backends (ubi, cargo, npm, aqua), Lua plugins, shell hooks, migrating from asdf/nvm/direnv, or debugging with mise doctor.

catalog.name: notify
catalog.description: Cross-platform notification system for Pi. Use notify_user when you need to urgently alert the user about critical findings, errors, or completion of long-running tasks.

catalog.name: plan
catalog.description: Strategic planning — create implementation plan from brainstorm specs. Tasks, dependencies, acceptance criteria.

catalog.name: ponytail
catalog.description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works, simplest, shortest, most minimal. Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests (general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, recipes).

catalog.name: ponytail-audit
catalog.description: Whole-repo audit for over-engineering. Like ponytail-review, but scans the entire codebase instead of a diff: a ranked list of what to delete, simplify, or replace with stdlib/native equivalents. Use when the user says "audit this codebase", "audit for over-engineering", "what can I delete from this repo", "find bloat", "ponytail-audit", or "/ponytail-audit". One-shot report, does not apply fixes.

catalog.name: ponytail-debt
catalog.description: Harvest every `ponytail:` comment in the codebase into a debt ledger, so the deliberate shortcuts and deferrals ponytail leaves behind get tracked instead of rotting into "later means never". Use when the user says "ponytail debt", "/ponytail-debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", "ponytail ledger", or "what did we mark to do later". One-shot report, changes nothing.

catalog.name: ponytail-gain
catalog.description: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, more speed, from the benchmark medians. One-shot display, not a persistent mode, and not a per-repo number. Trigger: /ponytail-gain, "ponytail gain", "what does ponytail save", "show ponytail impact", "ponytail scoreboard".

catalog.name: ponytail-help
catalog.description: Quick-reference card for all ponytail modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "what ponytail commands", "how do I use ponytail".

catalog.name: ponytail-review
catalog.description: Code review focused exclusively on over-engineering. Finds what to delete: reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, dead flexibility. One line per finding: location, what to cut, what replaces it. Use when the user says "review for over-engineering", "what can we delete", "is this over-engineered", "simplify review", or invokes /ponytail-review. Complements correctness-focused review, this one only hunts complexity.

catalog.name: quick-fix
catalog.description: Fast bug fix without debug report. One-shot fix for clear, simple bugs. Records fixes in docs/fix/.

catalog.name: quick-work
catalog.description: Fast single-task execution — one shot, done. Use for small tasks that don't need full brainstorm/plan/work flow.

catalog.name: release-notes
catalog.description: Write user-facing release notes from git history. Use when preparing a release or changelog.

catalog.name: research
catalog.description: Read-only research with bash access. Deep codebase investigation, documentation review, external research.

catalog.name: review-work
catalog.description: Review work — check task completion, run lint/build, mark reviewer remarks. Use after /unipi:work completes.

catalog.name: scan-issues
catalog.description: Passive codebase scan — find potential bugs, anti-patterns, security issues. Spawns subagents if available.

catalog.name: sql-review
catalog.description: Review SQL migrations for locking, indexes and rollback safety. Use before merging schema changes.

catalog.name: teach
catalog.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

catalog.name: to-questionnaire
catalog.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

catalog.name: unipi-subagents

Use for advisory review, implementation handoffs, and multi-step tasks where a single agent should stay in control while other agents contribute context, planning, or execution.

catalog.name: unipi-v3-development
catalog.description: Context and working state for unipi v3 development (the `v3` branch of the @pi-unipi extension suite). Use this skill at the start of ANY session that touches unipi v3: continuing the long-horizon module, the workspace/state de-scatter, the settings hub, per-package rewrites/removals, footer/badge UX, the network judge, or the v3-tasks plan. It records what is already done, the key architectural decisions, the gotchas that cost real debugging time, and where to look. Do NOT redo completed work — search here and docs/v3-tasks.md first.

catalog.name: wait-what

catalog.name: web
